video_title: Keys to the Cavs avoiding a sweep in series vs. the Knicks 🔑 | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Kenny Atkinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson discusses analytics and "expected score" despite losses
quotes.excerpt: Analytically, I think we won the expect I said three out of three, we're two out of three in the expected.
quotes.quote: Analytically, I think we won the expect I said three out of three, we're two out of three in the expected. I don't know if you guys follow that. There's an expected score, and we won two out of the three. And I know you're looking confused, but I there is really, if you believe in process and all that, like, man, our. So, you know, I take that layer. I know I don't throw that on them. I see it for myself. I'm like, man.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Iman Shumpert dismisses analytics, emphasizing losses and need for effort
quotes.excerpt: The only analytic is three L's in the column. That's it. I get it. I'm all about instilling confidence.
quotes.quote: The only analytic is three L's in the column. That's it. I get it. I'm all about instilling confidence in the guys, but they don't need confidence, they need a foot in their ass. This is bad. It hasn't been the energy, the effort hasn't been there, and that's what you that's what you yell at. You can't yell at mistakes, you can't yell at people being aggressive, you can't yell at missing shots.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst explains Cavaliers' "expected score" analytics, but Iman Shumpert dismisses it
quotes.excerpt: What Kenny was referring to was what he called expected score, which is some sort of something the Cavs must cook up.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: So what Kenny was referring to was what he called expected score, which is some sort of something the Cavs must cook up inside the building there. What he's talking about about luck, basically, can you quantify luck? This is what teams try to do. And so what if you look at the shooting percentages in this series, the expected shooting percentages, the Cavs and Knicks have basically generated the same quality of shots. What it's saying is in a laboratory, if you took the same shots, the Knicks would shoot 51% and the Cavs would shoot 52%. This is what Kenny is talking about.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: But he's saying, look, the Knicks are making 58% of those shots, and we're only making 50%. Therefore, they've been slightly lucky, and we've been slightly unlucky.

text_blocks.speaker: Iman Shumpert
text_blocks.text: They ain't been lucky. They just one team's playing defense and not letting you all make the shots. One team's not letting you all make the shots. The other team is letting it happen.

quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Iman Shumpert and Danny Green argue effort and defense outweigh fatigue and analytics for Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: Computer can't read tired legs. They can't read the eyes either because I don't see the confidence that James was just talking about.

text_blocks.speaker: Iman Shumpert
text_blocks.text: Exactly. They can't read the eyes either because I don't see the confidence that James was just talking about in the interview. I don't see it. I played in the league. I know what's going on in this arena. They want to see it too. Where the passion at?

text_blocks.speaker: Danny Green
text_blocks.text: I get what Kenny's saying. He's trying to look at some of the positives and instill some of that empowerment into his group. But this group has got to give it some. There was too many plays that were unacceptable where Jalen Brunson gets down the lane and lays the ball up. You got to show some pride. They got to come out like they did. It might be fatigue, but at this point, we don't want to hear fatigue at this point in the season. You got to come out, have the mental fortitude, the physical fortitude to actually compete and have a sense of urgency like you did in Game 7 in Detroit. You got to be aggressive, you got to be assertive, and you got to make shots. The reason why those analytical numbers Cleveland looks uncomfortable on offense because New York is playing defense. New York is they making those shots because they look more comfortable. They're swinging the ball, moving each other to each other and trusting each other. Cleveland has to do the same thing to get back into the series.

quotes.speaker: Karl-Anthony Towns
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns states the Knicks have new standards and expectations after last season
quotes.excerpt: It was historical last year, the city went crazy, and it was awesome to see the city so alive, but there's new standards now.
quotes.quote: It was historical last year, the city went crazy, and it was awesome to see the city so alive, but there's new standards now. There's new expectations, and we've raised the expectations. So we we knew what we came in this this season to do and what we wanted to accomplish, and we just got to keep our head down and continue to focus on the goal ahead.

quotes.speaker: Iman Shumpert
quotes.summary_phrase: Iman Shumpert criticizes Cavaliers' lack of defensive effort and communication against the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: It doesn't look like the Cavs have a bad game plan. It just looks like the effort has dropped off.
quotes.quote: I honestly don't. I think it needs to be an effort thing. It doesn't look like the Cavs have a bad game plan. It just looks like the effort has dropped off. Look at this right here. No man's land. James Harden, who are you guarding? We have to be able to force into these actions. Have a hand on a guy. If you are switching off a guy, be able to push that guy into the next guy that's picking him up. Have some communication. Declare the ball. Who's declared the ball right here? Okay, we got James Harden declaring the ball. Jalen Brunson going to come and get the ball. Again, indecision comes when they come together because they're not switching to attack. They are just switching because it's part of the game plan. Now we got Donovan Mitchell, token defense. One-two dribble blow by, it's token defense. You can't really ask for help in those situations. You got to put the ball handler under duress.
